edges.reason: Constructor assigns the token_ parameter to the immutable _token state variable.
Constructor assigns the beneficiary_ parameter to the immutable _beneficiary state variable.
Constructor assigns the releaseTime_ parameter to the immutable _releaseTime state variable.
Require(releaseTime_ > block.timestamp) makes the constructor outcome depend on the miner-controllable timestamp.
release() is gated by require(block.timestamp >= releaseTime()), a timestamp-dependent authorization check.
releaseTime() returns the _releaseTime state variable.
release() reads releaseTime() to decide whether the caller may withdraw, coupling authorization to block.timestamp.
token() returns the _token state variable.
beneficiary() returns the _beneficiary state variable.
release() calls token() to obtain the ERC20 contract it will interact with.
beneficiary() supplies the destination address of the external safeTransfer call in release().
token() supplies the external contract address that is invoked by the safeTransfer in release().
The immutable _token state variable determines the untrusted contract called during release().
release() executes an external token transfer, handing control to an untrusted token contract.
The local amount in release() is obtained from token().balanceOf(address(this)).
The locally computed amount is passed to the external safeTransfer call.
getLockedAmount() reads its balance through token().
safeTransfer delegates the actual token interaction to _callOptionalReturn.
_callOptionalReturn performs a low-level call on the token address, transferring control to an untrusted contract.
functionCallWithValue forwards value and calldata to an arbitrary target via a low-level call.
sendValue forwards ETH through a full-gas low-level call to recipient.
functionCallWithValue requires isContract(target) before performing the low-level call.
The recipient parameter becomes the callee of the low-level ETH transfer.
The amount parameter is attached as value to the low-level ETH transfer.
The target parameter is the callee of the low-level call.
The data parameter is forwarded as calldata of the low-level call.
The value parameter is attached as value to the low-level call.
The token parameter is the ERC20 instance whose transfer selector is encoded by safeTransfer.
The to parameter becomes the transfer recipient encoded by safeTransfer.
The value parameter becomes the transfer amount encoded by safeTransfer.
The success boolean local is assigned from the low-level ETH transfer result.
The size local is assigned from extcodesize inside isContract.
The external callee of sendValue can reenter the library function before the require(success) check completes.
The untrusted target can reenter functionCallWithValue while the low-level call is executing.
A malicious token contract can reenter _callOptionalReturn during the low-level call.
The token contract invoked by release() can call back into release() since no state is updated and no reentrancy guard is present.
